package_info.package_versions: Windows and MacOS builds affected in March-April 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp was compromised in a supply chain attack, resulting in the delivery of multiple malware payloads (TAXHAUL/TxRLoader, COLDCAT, SIMPLESEA) that enabled unauthorized code execution, persistence, and remote command-and-control, all without user consent. The attack leveraged DLL side-loading, in-memory shellcode execution, and installation of backdoors, impacting both Windows and MacOS platforms.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: TAXHAUL (TxRLoader) decrypts and executes shellcode from <machine hardware profile GUID>.TxR.0.regtrans-ms
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (post-installation, on application launch), the TAXHAUL loader reads an encrypted payload from C:\Windows\System32\config\TxR\<machine hardware profile GUID>.TxR.0.regtrans-ms, decrypts the shellcode in memory, and executes it, resulting in the in-memory launch of a downloader (COLDCAT) that can fetch additional payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Decrypting and executing shellcode from a hidden file in a system directory is highly anomalous and indicative of malicious intent, as legitimate applications do not perform such actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not execute code from files in the TxR directory, nor should it decrypt and run arbitrary shellcode at runtime from obscure system locations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security or update tools may use encrypted payloads for self-updating, but they do not use the TxR directory or execute arbitrary shellcode in this manner.
key_indicators: Decryption and execution of shellcode from a non-standard file location (TxR directory)
Use of system directories to conceal payloads
In-memory execution to evade disk-based detection
Access to and modification of files in C:\Windows\System32\config\TxR\

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: COLDCAT downloader (shellcode) connects to C2 domains (e.g., azureonlinecloud[.]com, akamaicontainer[.]com, journalide[.]org, msboxonline[.]com) to fetch additional payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the TAXHAUL loader executes the decrypted shellcode in memory, the COLDCAT downloader establishes outbound network connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains, retrieves additional malicious payloads, and executes them without user interaction.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected outbound connections to suspicious, attacker-controlled domains from a desktop application are highly anomalous and indicative of command-and-control activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate desktop applications should not connect to unlisted or suspicious C2 infrastructure, nor should they download and execute arbitrary code from such sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may contact update servers, but only to known, trusted domains and not to unlisted or suspicious C2 endpoints.
key_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 domains (azureonlinecloud[.]com, akamaicontainer[.]com, journalide[.]org, msboxonline[.]com)
Dynamic retrieval and execution of additional payloads
No user interaction required for network activity
Network activity initiated by in-memory shellcode

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on MacOS, post-installation or application launch)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SIMPLESEA MacOS backdoor located at /Library/Graphics/Quartz (MD5: d9d19abffc2c7dac11a16745f4aea44f)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (post-installation or application launch on MacOS), the SIMPLESEA backdoor binary executes from /Library/Graphics/Quartz, establishes persistence, and provides remote access and command execution capabilities to the attacker by communicating with C2 infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A binary masquerading as a graphics library in a non-standard location with a known malicious hash is highly suspicious and indicative of a backdoor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not drop or execute unauthorized binaries in /Library/Graphics/Quartz, nor should they provide remote access to attackers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for a binary to be present in /Library/Graphics/Quartz; this is not a standard location for system or application binaries.
key_indicators: Backdoor functionality enabling remote access and command execution

execution_context.file_location: DLL loaded via side-loading in the context of legitimate Microsoft Windows binaries

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious DLL side-loaded by legitimate Windows binaries to execute TAXHAUL malware.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application launch, a malicious DLL is side-loaded by a trusted Windows binary, resulting in the execution of attacker-controlled code (TAXHAUL) within the context and privileges of the legitimate process, establishing persistence and enabling further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL side-loading is a well-known technique for evading detection and achieving persistence by abusing the trust of legitimate processes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not load unauthorized DLLs, especially those that execute malware or alter process behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may use DLL injection for debugging or instrumentation, but not for executing unauthorized or malicious code.
key_indicators: DLL side-loading by trusted Windows binaries
Execution of malware in the context of legitimate processes
Persistence via hijacked or unauthorized DLLs
Abuse of Windows DLL search order

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL is side-loaded by a legitimate Windows binary, executing TAXHAUL (TxRLoader) malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Decryption and execution of shellcode from TxR directory

attack_chain.action: TAXHAUL decrypts and executes shellcode from <machine hardware profile GUID>.TxR.0.regtrans-ms.
COLDCAT downloader establishes outbound connections to C2 domains and fetches additional payloads.
On MacOS, SIMPLESEA backdoor is installed and provides remote access to attackers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and remote control on MacOS systems

behavioral_signatures: DLL side-loading by legitimate Windows binaries, especially those not typically loading external DLLs
Decryption and execution of shellcode from files in C:\Windows\System32\config\TxR\
Outbound network connections to suspicious C2 domains from desktop application processes
Presence and execution of unauthorized binaries in /Library/Graphics/Quartz on MacOS
In-memory execution of shellcode not present on disk
file_indicators: Unexpected DLLs loaded by trusted Windows binaries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLL side-loading activity by legitimate Windows binaries, especially those loading unauthorized DLLs. Detect decryption and execution of shellcode from files in the TxR directory. Alert on outbound connections to known C2 domains (azureonlinecloud[.]com, akamaicontainer[.]com, journalide[.]org, msboxonline[.]com) from desktop application processes. On MacOS, flag the presence and execution of binaries in /Library/Graphics/Quartz, especially with the known malicious MD5 hash. Correlate these behaviors for high-confidence detection of this supply chain attack, and prioritize alerts where multiple indicators are observed in sequence.
